findings: Organizer continues after per-file failures and returns successful move count with skippedCount, preserving healthy work. However skippedCount is assigned only after persistence and the all-failed throw, so failed runs can retain the previous count.
Moves happen before store.append. Persistence failure throws after filesystem effects without rollback or durable write-ahead intent, leaving moves without recorded undo history.
Undo verifies destination existence and original-path absence only, not physical identity or content. A replacement file at the recorded destination can be moved as if it were the original.

Missing undo sources are silently dropped from history, whereas conflicting original paths and move failures are retained for retry. History persistence happens after undo effects and can fail separately.
uniqueDestination probes sequential suffixes without bound or atomic reservation. moveItem itself can refuse a race collision; no overwrite guarantee beyond Foundation behavior was tested.
Profile folder names are appended directly and existing folders get a managed marker before movement. Containment and profile validation remain to be reviewed.

Persistence uses atomic whole-file JSON writes and caps move batches at 50; decisions are batched and explicitly prunable. Invalid/unreadable stored JSON silently becomes empty state and later writes may replace it. No corruption diagnostic or schema-version field is supplied here.

Actor methods serialize local mutation until awaiting store calls, but cross-actor organization/undo calls can interleave at those suspension points. No concurrency or file operation control was executed in this batch.
